title: pointerDown / pointerUp
description: A button transition, carrying the position it happened at so it never depends on a move arriving first. Must-arrive at app level: the host synthesises a press for an orphan pointerUp, releases held buttons after a silence (deadman), and releases everything when the channel closes -- a stuck button is the worst failure this milestone can produce. `inPlace` is game mode's: the host presses where its cursor already is instead of moving to nx/ny first, because a game that re-centres the cursor would read that move as a camera jump.

button.description: Which button changed. Only `left` is produced at M2; right and middle are in the schema because the host translation is generic over the enum, so the gestures that emit them are a phone-side change alone.

clickCount.description: 1 single, 2 double, 3 triple. THE PHONE DECIDES THIS, not the host: tap timing and finger travel are gesture context the phone has and the host would have to re-derive across a lossy channel. macOS needs it as kCGMouseEventClickState -- two plain clicks in a row do NOT register as a double-click in most apps.

inPlace.description: Press or release at the host's current cursor position, ignoring nx/ny for positioning. Absent means false: move there first, as a tap on a desktop app needs. Sent by game mode, where the host cursor has been moved by deltas and the phone no longer knows where it is.
